sections.h2: Which sale routes are open to an Aventura owner?
sections.html:
Condominium living means the building adds a step to each choice: an agent, a private deal or a cash buyer. The city's own description is an upscale condo community with large, well-known condominium and apartment buildings.

Before you choose, gather your association's documents and ask what approvals a buyer needs. Cash skips lender rules, though an association may still screen the buyer.

  • Through an agent: financed buyers and association approvals.
  • Directly: you arrange the contract and closing agent.
  • For cash: a closing day that suits your move.

sections.h2: What is Aventura like for a seller to describe?
sections.html:
Aventura is a compact city of 3.2 square miles on the Intracoastal Waterway in northeast Miami-Dade County. It was incorporated in 1995 as one of the county's newest municipalities, and the city places itself between two major South Florida airports and two of the largest seaports in the world.

The city says downtown Fort Lauderdale and Miami are about 20 minutes away, and that the Aventura Mall, restaurants and theaters are close by. Those travel times are useful selling points for a unit, because buyers often weigh waterfront access and commute together.

Families are part of the picture too. The city opened the first municipal-run charter school in Miami-Dade County, Aventura City of Excellence School, in fall 2003. The city says it serves 900 children from kindergarten to 8th grade, and it sits next to a 25,000 square foot community and recreation center on 2.8 waterfront acres. The Government Center houses commission chambers, the police station and administrative offices in one place, which is handy when you need city records.

sections.h2: How does Miami-Dade County property tax apply to an Aventura sale?
sections.html:
The Miami-Dade Property Appraiser values property but does not send tax bills or set taxes, so questions about a bill go to the Miami-Dade Tax Collector. The appraiser certified the 2026 tax roll on October 16, 2026, a date now behind us, so 2026 values stand unless the Value Adjustment Board changes them after hearings.

The appraiser's June estimate put the countywide taxable value at $540.7 billion for 2026, up 5.5 percent from 2025, which shows the pressure on values that your buyer will see. Its office takes calls at 305-375-4712, and applications for widow and widower exemptions and for veteran disability exemptions can be filed online.

Property tax roles in Miami-Dade for an Aventura owner
OfficeWhat it does
Property AppraiserSets assessments; does not bill or collect
Tax CollectorSends bills and collects payment
Clerk of Court and ComptrollerRecords deeds and offers a free property fraud alert
Value Adjustment BoardHears petitions; value challenges are due within 25 days of the August notice

sections.h2: What state homestead rules should an Aventura seller know?
sections.html:
Homestead relief reaches $50,000 of value for owners who applied by March 1. Save Our Homes keeps annual assessment growth at or under inflation, never above 3 percent, and the state's 2026 figure is 2.7 percent.

A sale or any other transfer of title resets the property to market value on the next January 1, so your buyer's first bill may look much higher than yours. Portability can carry part of your savings to a new Florida homestead set up inside the three year window the Department of Revenue guide describes. Renting the unit or moving out ends the homestead, so skip a long rental between listing and closing.

Other state benefits may matter to the person you sell to or to you. An ordinance may allow owners aged 65 or more an added homestead exemption of up to $50,000 within an income limit, a disabled ex-servicemember may receive a $5,000 reduction in assessed value, and veterans 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability may receive a homestead discount equal to the VA disability percentage. Ask the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser which of these apply to the unit.

Bills arrive in November, discounted 4 percent at first and 1 percent by February, and unpaid ones go delinquent April 1.

sections.h2: How are deed taxes different in Miami-Dade?
sections.html:
Miami-Dade stands apart on deed tax: 60 cents per $100, plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax that does not apply to a document moving only a single-family dwelling. Other counties charge 70 cents.

Every party to the deed answers to the state for the tax, so the contract should name who covers it. The exception is worded for single-family dwellings, so ask the clerk or your closing agent how a condominium unit is treated before you price the sale. Recording charges at the clerk are set by statute per page. Deeds need two subscribing witnesses.

A lady bird deed, according to a Department of Revenue advisement, did not transfer present beneficial interests on the facts presented and was not subject to doc stamp tax. That ruling applies to specific facts, so get advice before using one.

sections.h2: What protects an Aventura owner from deed fraud?
sections.html:
The Miami-Dade clerk runs a no-cost alert system that emails you within 24 hours of a deed or mortgage being filed under your name. The property appraiser's office also takes homestead fraud reports at 305-375-3402.

If you hold an empty unit while selling, sign up for the alert and check that the mailing address on file is current so notices reach you.

The appraiser's offices are at the Stephen P. Clark Center in downtown Miami and at the South Dade Government Center in Cutler Bay, and appointments can be booked online. Bring the deed and any exemption paperwork if you need a record corrected before closing.

sections.h2: What should an Aventura owner check before accepting an offer?
sections.html:
Start with the building. Ask the association for its financial statements, pending assessments and approval rules, then compare the price against what the appraiser shows for the folio. The property record lists assessments, exemptions and sales, and the appraiser's tax estimator tutorial explains how a buyer can estimate a bill.

  • Payoff letters from every lender or lien holder on the unit.
  • Proof of exemptions you hold, since a sale ends your homestead on that unit.
  • Confirmation of who pays deed tax in the contract.
  • The Tax Collector's balance for the year.

If a tenant lives in the unit, Florida requires a written three day notice, not counting weekends and court holidays, to end a non-payment tenancy. A foreclosure judgment sets the sale 20 to 35 days later, and Florida allows summary administration for an estate of $150,000 or less. Any of these can change your timeline, so talk to a Florida attorney early.

faqs.q: Does Aventura have its own property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Miami-Dade Tax Collector sends the bill. The appraiser sets values and neither bills nor sets rates.

faqs.q: What is the deed stamp tax in Aventura?
faqs.a: Miami-Dade charges 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax. The surtax is not due on a document transferring only a single-family dwelling, so ask how it treats a condo unit.

faqs.q: When did Aventura become a city?
faqs.a: Aventura was incorporated in 1995, according to the city. It covers 3.2 square miles on the Intracoastal Waterway in northeast Miami-Dade County.

faqs.q: Can a cash buyer purchase an Aventura condo as-is?
faqs.a: Often yes, but the condo association may have its own approval process, so read your documents and ask the association before you commit to a closing date.

faqs.q: How do I protect against deed fraud when I sell?
faqs.a: Sign up for the Miami-Dade Clerk's free property fraud alert, which notifies you within 24 hours when a document is recorded in your name.
